narrative.overview:
Every vacancy is a departure. It has a Ref, a destination city, a closing time and a live status, and the site reads like the flight-information displays and wayfinding of an international terminal. Drenched board blue owns whole regions of the page (the Openings board, the job-detail header, the employer field, the footer); terminal white and cool concourse grey carry the reading; hairline rules divide everything else. Hierarchy comes from type scale and region colour. There are no decorative containers.

The register is professional, calm and exact. Fixed-width mono cells carry the machine facts (refs, times, counts, statuses) and settle into place with a split-flap motion. Display headlines are heavy and tightly tracked. Body copy is plain and generous. Amber is the only warm colour, and it appears only when a vacancy is about to close.

The system is a deliberate refusal of the job-portal category default: no dark photo hero with a rounded search pill, no pastel icon tiles, no card-shell listings.
keyCharacteristics: Board blue fills whole regions. It is never used as a tint wash or gradient.
Hairline rules (1px) and ruled sequences take the place of cards and tiles.
Mono flap cells with a hinge line for refs, closing days and result counts.
Square forms: 4px for controls and panels, 2px for cells and status tags.
Amber means closing time and nothing else.
Photography bleeds to the edge or fills a whole panel. It is never a framed thumbnail.

rules.name: The Amber Means Leaving Rule
rules.body: Amber appears only on the Closing and Final call statuses. It is never used for decoration, highlights, buttons or brand accents.

rules.name: The Region Rule
rules.body: Blue arrives as a whole region (a section, a header or a panel), not as a tinted card or a gradient. A screen alternates fields of white or grey with fields of blue.

rules.name: The No-Green Rule
rules.body: The palette has no green token. Status runs NEW (sky/blue), OPEN (outlined), CLOSING (amber outline or soft), FINAL CALL (solid amber).

rules.name: The Machine Facts Rule
rules.body: Anything a departures board would print (Ref, time, count, days, status) is set in Red Hat Mono with tabular numerals. Human prose is never set in mono.

rules.name: The Uppercase Belongs to the Tags Rule
rules.body: Uppercase is used only in status tags. Headings, job titles, labels and buttons stay in sentence case.

rules.name: The Hung Not Floating Rule
rules.body: A shadow is allowed only when a surface overlaps photography or the page as an overlay. Listings and in-flow panels sit flat on their ground.

dos: **Do** let Board Blue (#0b2a7a) and Board Blue Deep (#061a4d) fill whole regions, alternating with white and grey (#eef1f6) bands.
**Do** set every Ref, time, count, day figure and status in Red Hat Mono with tabular numerals.
**Do** use the split-flap settle for board facts (Ref, Closes, result counts), and always render the final text under reduced motion.
**Do** divide content with 1px hairlines (#d9dfea) and ruled sequences, and build hierarchy from type scale and region colour.
**Do** keep corners square: 4px for controls and panels, 2px for cells and tags.
**Do** use field labels in sentence case, small, at weight 700, in ink-3 (#5a6680) above values, the way the kiosk does.
**Do** show a photograph only where the subject has a real one. Otherwise use a blue signage panel.
donts: **Don't** use amber (#f2b632) for anything except the Closing and Final call statuses.
**Don't** wrap listings in cards, add shadows to rows or in-flow panels, or put thumbnails on vacancy rows.
**Don't** use rounded pill search bars, pill tags or circular badges.
**Don't** use icon tiles: pastel squares or circles holding an icon to decorate a feature, step or sector.
**Don't** put an uppercase eyebrow or kicker label above section headings. Section headings stand alone.
**Don't** introduce green, gradients or tinted-blue card washes.
**Don't** set prose or headings in mono, or use uppercase outside the board grammar and status tags.
